arxiv-2108-01303.title: A twin-jet structure rather than jet-rotation in the young stellar object OMC 2/FIR 6b
arxiv-2108-01303.creator: Noam Soker, Jesse Bublitz, Joel H. Kastner
arxiv-2108-01303.description: Abstract We analyse recent high-quality Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) molecular line mapping observations of the northeast jet of the young stellar object (YSO) OMC 2/FIR 6b (HOPS-60) and find that these ALMA observations are much more likely to indicate a twin-jet structure than jet rotation, as previously hypothesized.

arxiv-2112-11457.title: Simulation of many body localization and time crystals in two dimensions with the neighborhood tensor update
arxiv-2112-11457.creator: Jacek Dziarmaga
arxiv-2112-11457.description: Abstract The Heisenberg antiferromagnet with discrete disorder on an infinite square lattice is evolved in time from an initial Néel state. The simulation is performed with the neighborhood tensor update (NTU) algorithm for an infinite projected entangled pair state (iPEPS) [Phys. Rev. B 104, 094411 (2021)].

arxiv-2204-10236.title: The average size of maximal matchings in graphs
arxiv-2204-10236.creator: Alain Hertz, Sébastien Bonte, Gauvain Devillez, Hadrien Mélot, [3mm] Department of Mathematics, Industrial Engineering Polytechnique Montréal - Gerad, Montréal, CanadaCorresponding author. Email: alain.hertz@gerad.ca, [3mm] Computer Science Department - Algorithms LabUniversity of Mons, Mons, Belgiu
arxiv-2204-10236.description: Abstract Abstract. We investigate the ratio \mathcal{I}(G) of the average size of a maximal matching to the size of a maximum matching in a graph G . If many maximal matchings have a size close to \nu(G) , this graph invariant has a value close to 1. Conversely, if many maximal matchings have a small size, \mathcal{I}(G) approaches \frac{1}{2} .

arxiv-2207-02320.title: Tricritical behavior in a neural model with excitatory and inhibitory units
arxiv-2207-02320.creator: Joaquin Almeira, Tomas S. Grigera, Dante R. Chialvo, Sergio A. Cannas
arxiv-2207-02320.description: Abstract While the support for the relevance of critical dynamics to brain function is increasing, there is much less agreement on the exact nature of the advocated critical point. Thus, a considerable number of theoretical efforts are currently concentrated on which mechanisms and what type/s of transition can be exhibited by neuronal networks models.

arxiv-2306-09224.title: Encyclopedic VQA: Visual questions about detailed properties of fine-grained categories
arxiv-2306-09224.creator: Thomas Mensink mensink@google.com, Jasper Uijlings jrru@google.com, Lluis Castrejon lluisc@google.com, Arushi Goel goel.arushi@gmail.com, Felipe Cadar cadar@dcc.ufmg.br, Howard Zhou howardzhou@google.com, Fei Sha fsha@google.com, André Araujo andrearaujo@google.com, Vittorio Ferrari vittoferrari@goo
arxiv-2306-09224.description: Abstract We propose Encyclopedic -VQA, a large scale visual question answering (VQA) dataset featuring visual questions about detailed properties of fine-grained categories and instances. It contains 221k unique question+answer pairs each matched with (up to) 5 images, resulting in a total of 1M VQA samples.

arxiv-2312-02392.title: Instance Space Analysis of Search-Based Software Testing
arxiv-2312-02392.creator: Neelofar Neelofar, Kate Smith-Miles, Mario Andrés Muñoz, Aldeida Aleti
arxiv-2312-02392.description: Abstract Search-based software testing (SBST) is now a mature area, with numerous techniques developed to tackle the challenging task of software testing. SBST techniques have shown promising results and have been successfully applied in the industry to automatically generate test cases for large and complex software systems. Their effectiveness, however, has been shown to be problem dependent.

arxiv-2403-05723.title: Digital Wellbeing Redefined: Toward User-Centric Approach for Positive Social Media Engagement Conference: IEEE/ACM 11th International Conference on Mobile Software Engineering and Systems; April 14–15, 2024; Lisbon, Portugal IEEE/ACM 11th International Conference on Mobile Software Engineering and
arxiv-2403-05723.creator: Yixue Zhao, Tianyi Li, Michael Sobolev
arxiv-2403-05723.description: Abstract . The prevalence of social media and its escalating impact on mental health has highlighted the need for effective digital wellbeing strategies. Current digital wellbeing interventions have primarily focused on reducing screen time and social media use, often neglecting the potential benefits of these platforms.

arxiv-2412-16105.title: Quantifying the benefit of load uncertainty reduction for the design of district energy systems under grid constraints using the Value of Information
arxiv-2412-16105.creator: Max Langtry, Ruchi Choudhary
arxiv-2412-16105.description: Abstract Load uncertainty must be accounted for during design to ensure building energy systems can meet energy demands during operation. Reducing building load uncertainty allows for improved designs with less compromise to be identified, reducing the cost of decarbonizing energy usage. However, the building monitoring required to reduce load uncertainty is costly.

arxiv-2509-02624.title: Who Owns The Robot?: Four Ethical and Socio-technical Questions about Wellbeing Robots in the Real World through Community Engagement
arxiv-2509-02624.creator: Minja Axelsson, Jiaee Cheong, Rune Nyrup, Hatice Gunes
arxiv-2509-02624.description: Abstract Recent studies indicated that robotic coaches can play a crucial role in promoting wellbeing. However, the real-world deployment of wellbeing robots raises numerous ethical and socio-technical questions and concerns. To explore these questions, we undertake a community-centered investigation to examine three different communities’ perspectives on the ethical questions related to using robotic wellbeing coaches in real-world environments.

arxiv-2602-05113.title: Democratic Preference Alignment via Sortition-Weighted RLHF
arxiv-2602-05113.creator: Suvadip Sana, Jinzhou Wu, Martin T. Wells
arxiv-2602-05113.description: Abstract Whose values should AI systems learn? Preference-based alignment methods like RLHF derive their training signal from human raters, yet these rater pools are typically convenience samples that systematically over-represent some demographics and under-represent others. We introduce Democratic Preference Optimization (DemPO), a framework that applies algorithmic sortition, the same mechanism used to construct citizen assemblies, to preference-based fine-tuning.

arxiv-2602-08327.title: Forced oscillation of a damped BBM equation posed on whole line in low regularity spaces
arxiv-2602-08327.creator: Chun-Ho Lau

The impact of these factors on the Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) measure has not been comprehensively evaluated.

pmc-10668738.description: Simple SummaryThis study focused on evaluating the impact of different alternative lipid sources in the diet of meat quails. The researchers investigated nutrient metabolism, performance, carcass characteristics, and meat quality. Two experiments were conducted, the first of which analyzed the energy values and metabolizability of various lipid sources.

pmc-10709747.title: Therapeutic drug monitoring to personalize dosing of imatinib, sunitinib, and pazopanib: A mixed methods study on barriers and facilitators
pmc-10709747.creator: Kim Westerdijk, Neeltje Steeghs, Casper S J Tacke, Winette T A van der Graaf, Nielka P van Erp, Gerard van Oortmerssen, Rosella P M G Hermens, Ingrid M E Desar, In collaboration with the Dutch Pharmacology Oncology Group (DPOG)
pmc-10709747.description: BackgroundPersonalized dosing based on measurement of individual drug levels and adjusting the dose accordingly can improve efficacy and decrease unnecessary toxicity of oncological treatment. For imatinib, sunitinib, and pazopanib, this therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)‐guided dosing is, however, not routinely used, despite accumulating evidence favoring individualized dosing.

pmc-10729028.title: What is the current global health participation and future interest of healthcare students and National Health Service (NHS) staff? A cross-sectional research study of healthcare students and NHS staff in England

pmc-11333703.title: Fabric soft pneumatic actuators with programmable turing pattern textures
pmc-11333703.creator: Masato Tanaka, Yuyang Song, Tsuyoshi Nomura
pmc-11333703.description: This paper presents a novel computational design and fabrication method for fabric-based soft pneumatic actuators (FSPAs) that use Turing patterns, inspired by Alan Turing’s morphogenesis theory. These inflatable structures can adapt their shapes with simple pressure changes and are applicable in areas like soft robotics, airbags, and temporary shelters.

pmc-11608070.title: Quantitative evaluation of the effects of several weeks of static stretching on the flexibility of the rectus femoris using shear wave elastography: a before–after study
pmc-11608070.creator: Bungo Ebihara, Hayato Miyasaka, Takashi Fukaya, Hirotaka Mutsuzaki
pmc-11608070.description: AimThe study aimed to quantitatively clarify the effects of several weeks of static stretching on the flexibility of the rectus femoris muscle using shear wave elastography.Material and methodsFifteen healthy men (age: 26.4 ± 2.2 years) were instructed to perform 5 min of voluntary static stretching of their right rectus femoris muscles five times a week for four weeks.

pmc-11644045.title: Nutri-Score in the European Food Retail Supply: A Potential Incentive for Food Reformulation?
pmc-11644045.creator: Elly Steenbergen, Joline W J Beulens, Elisabeth H M Temme, Roberto Iacone
pmc-11644045.description: Background: To improve consumers’ diet, policy measures such as food reformulation strategies and front-of-pack nutritional labels (FOPNLs) are implemented, aiming to guide consumers’ food choice and to stimulate an improvement in food composition by manufacturers. The FOPNL Nutri-Score has been implemented in several European countries. Changes in food compositions in relation to the Nutri-Score over time have been limitedly studied.

pmc-13076879.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Glacial lake outburst floods (jökulhlaups) are challenging to study because they often take place below hundreds of meters of ice, and the complex interplay between lifting of the glacier and melting of the flood path is not well understood.

pmc-13193671.title: A Practical Approach to Assessing the Completeness of Electronic Health Records for Medical Research: Data Quality Study
pmc-13193671.creator: Minsik Lim, Doyeon An, Nayeong Son, Woongsang Sunwoo, Suehyun Lee
pmc-13193671.description: BackgroundData quality is the degree to which data are fit for their intended purpose and is described using quality dimensions. The increased use of medical data in clinical research and medical artificial intelligence development has rendered data quality assessment essential. Despite existing data quality definitions, frameworks, and tools, data quality assessment in real-world settings faces multiple challenges.

pmc-13233658.title: Aging-related lateral ventricular shape changes and corresponding mechanical loading derived from longitudinal image registration
pmc-13233658.creator: Lauren Cunniff, Johannes Weickenmeier, the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
pmc-13233658.description: Lateral ventricular enlargement is one of the most prominent features of the aging brain and is clearly visible on structural magnetic resonance imaging. Both longitudinal and cross-sectional imaging studies have shown that ventricular volume progressively increases with age and expands even faster in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.

pmc-13367339.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Models for Early Detection of Metabolic Dysfunction–Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Using Non-Invasive Routine Clinical and Laboratory Data
pmc-13367339.creator: Yuan-Hao You, Li-Yun Chen, Alexander Valley Chang, Yu-Shiang Lin
pmc-13367339.description: IntroductionThe purpose of this study was to develop and evaluate multiple interpretable machine learning models for the early detection of metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) using non-invasive routine clinical and laboratory data, with magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) as a quantitative reference standard, and to assess the feasibility of MRI-PDFF–calibrated risk stratification as a pre-screening approach

pmc-13457852.title: Discovery and quantification of novel diazepam metabolites BP-246 and BP-271 in freshwater fish using HRMS and UPLC-MS/MS
pmc-13457852.creator: Ping Ouyang, Junlin Wang, Nianhua Zhang, Zhengyan Hu, Changren Ye, Dingnan Wang, Yang Wang, Pinggu Wu
pmc-13457852.description: Diazepam, commonly used in freshwater fish transport and aquaculture, poses potential food safety and public health risks due to its residues and metabolites. However, current monitoring efforts primarily focus on the parent drug and its major metabolites, leaving potential toxic transformation products uncharacterized.
